name: telegram
description: Use Telegram through the venue's bots: send messages, media or buttons, understand Telegram-originated chats, and check bot status. Load for Telegram communication; it reveals separate bot-management guidance for creating, configuring or deleting bots.

content.inline:
## Telegram
A bot that acts as your identity is yours to use. Bot API fields retain snake_case; Covia storage options use destination and fileName.

- `send {bot?, chat_id, text, ...}` sends text. A private chat id is the person's Telegram user id; group ids are negative; channels may use `@channelusername`. Omit `bot` only when you own exactly one.
- `call {bot?, method, params, files?}` covers other Bot API methods such as sendPhoto, sendDocument, editMessageText, deleteMessage and answerCallbackQuery. Media may use a Telegram file_id, public URL or multipart files: `{voice:{ref:"dlfs/telegram/note.ogg",filename:"note.ogg"}}` for sendVoice. References resolve under your authority; total upload bytes are limited to 20 MiB.
- `download {bot?, file_id, destination?, fileName?}` returns {ref, fileName, size}, plus original file_name and contentType when known. Destination is a directory, e.g. dlfs/imports or file://inbox, with optional trailing slash. Omit it for the bot owner's private DLFS telegram drive. Name selection: explicit fileName, safe original name retained from an admitted message, then generated fallback. Conflicts use report(1).pdf without overwriting. getFile alone does not supply the original name. Explicit directories use your write authority and a provider supporting create-only writes; parent directories must exist. Reading requires provider read authority.
- `bots {}` lists the bots you may use, including state, username and any startup error; tokens are never returned.

Inbound messages arrive as `{text, via, attachments?, content?}`. Attachments carry kind, file_id, protected ref and mediaType; a configured mediaOperation may add extracted/transcribed text or application data under attachment.result, or return {} to pass media through. An optional replyOperation formats the agent response for Telegram (telegram/format turns Markdown into Telegram HTML). Images also arrive as image blocks. Without a transcription operation or tool, do not claim to have listened to audio. Forum topics have separate sessions; via retains topic, reply-message and media-group IDs. The venue supplies `via`: `from` is the Telegram-authenticated sender, `chat` the chat, `bot` the receiving bot and `access` either `allow` or `open`. This identifies a Telegram account, not a Covia principal, and grants no venue authority.

Rules:
- Never guess a chat id; use one supplied by the user or a received update.
- A bot with an allow list only messages the people on it: chat_id (and from_chat_id / user_id in call) must be a listed id or the account of a listed @username who has already written to the bot, and the bot ignores group chats. A refusal naming this rule is the venue enforcing it, not a fault; your reply in the current conversation is still delivered.
- Prefer plain, concise text. Use parse_mode only when needed; to send Markdown, convert it with telegram/format and send its text with the parse_mode it returns.
- Use inline keyboards for choices and acknowledge callback queries.
- A missing or PENDING bot may be fixable. When asked to create, register, configure, repair or delete a bot, load `telegram-bot-management` rather than claiming bot management is operator-only.
